items.evidence_text: Privilege escalation: After gaining execution as the web-service account, in few observed incidents, threat actors attempted to exploit CVE-2026-43284, one of the recent Linux kernel vulnerabilities also known as Dirty Frag, to elevate privileges to root.
items.create_eligibility_detail: No IOC creation expected for context-only or ignored indicators.

items.evidence_text: T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application | Internet-facing web applications were exploited to gain command execution in the web service context. Follow-on commands were launched as children of web server and application runtime processes, consistent with exploitation of an exposed application.
items.create_eligibility_detail: No IOC creation expected for context-only or ignored indicators.

items.evidence_text: T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell | Commands used curl to retrieve the GSocket installation script and executed it with bash.
items.create_eligibility_detail: No IOC creation expected for context-only or ignored indicators.

items.evidence_text: T1053.003 Scheduled Task/Job: Cron | Cron entries were created in the same detection window as GSocket deployment script activity, consistent with persistence.
items.create_eligibility_detail: No IOC creation expected for context-only or ignored indicators.

items.evidence_text: T1543.002 Create or Modify System Process: Systemd Service | Activity launched a bash command invoking the renamed /usr/bin/defunct payload and referenced defunct.service and a multi-user.target.wants link.
items.create_eligibility_detail: No IOC creation expected for context-only or ignored indicators.

items.evidence_text: T1036 Masquerading | A GsNetcat binary executed as systemd-remount-d, a system service-like filename. In a separate execution context, bash used exec -a to present /usr/bin/defunct with the argument-zero name [kaluad].
items.create_eligibility_detail: No IOC creation expected for context-only or ignored indicators.

items.evidence_text: T1564.001 Hide Artifacts: Hidden Files and Directories | gs-netcat payloads were staged under the dot-prefixed /dev/shm/.gs-0 directory. A GsNetcat-detected file was also observed at /tmp/.gsn_ora.
items.create_eligibility_detail: No IOC creation expected for context-only or ignored indicators.

items.evidence_text: T1222.002 File and Directory Permissions Modification: Linux and Mac File and Directory Permissions Modification | chmod changed permissions on the renamed payload, including chmod 700 /usr/bin/defunct.
items.create_eligibility_detail: No IOC creation expected for context-only or ignored indicators.

items.evidence_text: T1070.006 Indicator Removal: Timestomp | touch commands applied older timestamps to /usr/bin/defunct and defunct.service. Timestamp copy operations targeted the system service-like payload name.
items.create_eligibility_detail: No IOC creation expected for context-only or ignored indicators.

items.evidence_text: T1070.004 Indicator Removal: File Deletion | rm removed the staged /dev/shm/.gs-0/gs-netcat file, and a separate rmdir command removed the staging directory.
items.create_eligibility_detail: No IOC creation expected for context-only or ignored indicators.

items.evidence_text: T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer | curl downloaded gs-netcat payloads from GSocket distribution endpoints into /dev/shm/.gs-0.
items.create_eligibility_detail: No IOC creation expected for context-only or ignored indicators.

items.evidence_text: T1090.002 Proxy: External Proxy | GSocket clients were launched with options that establish outbound sessions to the Global Socket Relay Network, a shared public relay that brokers the connection between the compromised host and the operator. The relay is third-party infrastructure and is not owned by the threat actor.
items.create_eligibility_detail: No IOC creation expected for context-only or ignored indicators.
